title: Model signing key rotation — canary verification failure and rollback review
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the on-call notes, initial timeline, hypotheses, mitigations, and proposed runbook updates following the canary failure triggered during model signing key rotation on 2025-01-18. Canary hosts started rejecting new weight bundles due to signature verification errors which cascaded into degraded canary traffic and an automated rollback.

High-level impact:
- Affected path: canary fleet for model-v2.3 rollout in us-west1.
- User-facing impact: none observed (canaries only), but canary failures prevented phased rollout and blocked scheduled promoting of v2.3 to production.
- Duration: ~40 minutes from first failure to completion of controlled rollback.
- Severity: sev2 (blocked rollout, potential for wider impact if unnoticed).

Detection and alerting:
- 2025-01-18 09:07 UTC — Canary health probe alerts: 6/20 canaries failing model load with exit code 73 (VERIFICATION_FAILED). Alert routed to eng-sre, Pager duty paged.
- Automated promoter noticed >50% canary load verification failures and paused the staged rollout per policy. Slack alerts in #model-rollouts.

Immediate actions (on-call):
- 09:08 — on-call checked canary logs: verify_signature() returned mismatch checksum for weight-bundle id wb-2025-01-18-09.
- 09:11 — rolled back promoter state to previous signed bundle (wb-2025-01-12-22) to stop additional hosts from pulling the new bundle.
- 09:16 — kicked a small set of manual reloads on failed canaries to confirm rollback behavior; they reloaded successfully and returned to healthy.
- 09:26 — confirmed canary metrics recovered to expected baseline.

Observed symptoms and logs (selected):
- Worker logs: "Signature verification failed: expected sig v=1-abc123, got v=1-def456"
- Weight manifest entries included mismatched signing-key-id (rotated-key-2025-01-18) but signature blob was generated with legacy-key-2024-11.
- Artifact store (s3) showed two bundles uploaded within minutes; one bundle had correct manifest but signature entry did not match key-id field.

Initial hypotheses considered:
1) During key rotation, the signing service returned an old signature (race between rotation and cache population).
2) Upload pipeline attached the new key-id metadata but re-used a cached signature blob from the writer service.
3) Manifest signer and blob signer services were on different versions and had incompatible signing format after a code refactor.

Root cause (confirmed):
- Race condition in weight publish pipeline: the metadata update that set signing-key-id was applied before the signing worker finished writing a new signature. A retry path in the uploader re-bound metadata resulting in a manifest that claimed a different key than actually used to sign the blob. The verification library on canary nodes is strict and rejects any mismatch between key-id and signature algorithm/payload.

Why only canaries initially?
- Canary nodes fetch new bundles earlier than main pool (staggered); the set of canaries pulled the problematic bundle before the publisher detected and corrected the retry ordering for the upload flow. By the time main production hosts fetched, the publisher had completed a correct re-upload or the promoter paused further pushes, preventing production impact.

Mitigation timeline (what we did):
- Promotional pause and automated stop of rollout (09:09).
- Immediate rollback to previously signed bundle (09:11).
- Manual reloads and health checks (09:16–09:26).
- Disable automated signer rotation job until fix verified (09:30).
- Opened blocking PR to uploader to ensure atomic write of manifest+signature (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/weights/pull/189).

Runbook gaps discovered (notes):
- No explicit verification step in the publisher pipeline to validate manifest.key_id matches signature.key_id before marking bundle as 'published'.
- Monitoring lacked a specific metric for 'manifest/signature mismatch' — we only caught the symptom at canary-side verification errors.
- Rollback playbook assumed binary failure modes (bad weights or missing artifacts) but not metadata/signature mismatch.

Proposed short-term fixes (priority):
- Enforce atomic publish: only mark bundle published after end-to-end signing verification passes locally on the publisher. (owner: Marco; ETA: 48h)
- Add publisher-side self-check metric: bundle_publish.signature_mismatch{env,model} -> alert if >0 for any publish. (owner: Priya; ETA: 72h)
- Add post-publish signer audit job that verifies last N publishes keys and signatures (cron job). (owner: Ethan; ETA: 1 week)
- Re-enable rotation after test window and additional canary passes.

Longer-term process changes (follow-ups):
- Update rollout promoter to include a pre-promotion verification stage where a subset of canaries run a signature verification test before being counted healthy. (product + eng-sre)
- Documentation: add a 'Signing Key Rotation' checklist to Ops runbooks with explicit gating and rollback criteria. (owner: Janelle; ETA: 2 weeks)
- Add unit/integration tests around publisher retry logic and signature binding. (owner: serving-runtime infra; ETA: 3 weeks)

Concrete actions completed in this incident:
- Created blocking PR to ensure atomic publish.
- Paused rotation job and set a temporary protection on keys so no further rotations can be scheduled.
- Filed JIRA-INC-4321 tracking follow-ups.

How to reproduce (dev notes):
- Run local publisher with simulated intermittent blob signer that sometimes returns an older signature for a new artifact id; then flip metadata update order to simulate the race.
- Test local verification by spinning up canary-like process that runs verify_signature() with strict key-id enforcement.

Rollback playbook (draft) — add to runbook repo:
- If canaries fail with VERIFICATION_FAILED:
  1) Immediately pause promoter and block new bundle propagation.
  2) Confirm affected bundle id from logs (example: wb-2025-01-18-09).
  3) Pin promoter to last-known-good bundle id and force-reload canaries.
  4) If reloads succeed, leave rollout paused and run publisher integrity checks.
  5) If reload fails or production starts seeing failures, escalate to sev1 and follow production rollback steps.

Monitoring playbook additions (suggested alerts):
- New alert: manifest_signature_mismatch_rate > 0 over 1m for publisher cluster -> page eng-sre.
- Enhanced canary probe: if >20% of canaries in a group return VERIFICATION_FAILED over 2m, pause promoter and page.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we require signer and publisher to live in the same deployment boundary (reduce cross-service version skew)? Pros/cons discussion below.
- What's the acceptable downtime window for rotation maintenance? We need scheduling guidance for future rotations.

Appendix: raw investigator notes (chronological)
- 09:06:17 — auto-promoter triggered push for v2.3.
- 09:07:03 — first canary log: "verify_signature: mismatch key-id (rotated-key-2025-01-18) vs signature metadata (legacy-key-2024-11)"
- 09:09:00 — promoter paused automatically.
- 09:11:10 — pinned promoter to wb-2025-01-12-22.
- 09:12:45 — uploader logs show a retry loop 09:05:47–09:05:51 which wrote signature second, metadata updated at 09:05:50.
- 09:14:30 — manual reloads succeeded on 4/4 tested canaries.
- 09:29:00 — rotation job disabled (safety flag).

Owner notes / next meeting:
- We will do a postmortem review session on 2025-01-28 16:00 UTC with stakeholders from SRE, serving-runtime, and publishing infra. Agenda: timeline recap, root cause walkthrough, review PR, sign off on metric/alert changes, decide on post-rotation gating policy.

Draft status: this is a working incident review intended to capture facts and propose action items. Please add comments inline or push corrections to the ticket JIRA-INC-4321.

Tags for search: model-signing, key-rotation, canary-failure, rollback, publisher, verification
